belief: the model line goes Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable
corrected_statement: As of 22 October 2026 the belief is right about the four generally available Claude tiers but wrong as a description of the whole line and of its history. Anthropic's docs list four current models, Fable 5.1 (1 September 2026 per the docs release notes; $10/$50 per million input/output tokens), Opus 5.5 (22 September; $4/$20), Sonnet 5.5 (28 September; $2/$10) and Haiku 5.5 (7 October; from $0.10/$0.50), and Anthropic Academy calls them four tiers: Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku. The line does not end at Fable. Fable is a Mythos-class model, and Claude Mythos 5.1 is the same model at the same price with fewer cyber and biology safeguards, open only to organizations verified through Anthropic's programs; the Models API names five model lines (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, mythos) and claude.com labels the top family 'Mythos (including Fable)'. Mythos came first: its name leaked on 26 March 2026 (Fortune), Anthropic announced Mythos Preview on 7 April 2026, and Fable 5 launched on 9 June 2026. Anthropic's launch post said Mythos-class models sit above its Opus class, but its 22 September Opus 5.5 post says Opus 5.5 performs at Fable 5.1's level on most work and shows it ahead on all nine benchmarks in its table, while the docs still say to start with Opus 5.5 and move to Fable 5.1 when Opus evals fall short. The names are concurrent tiers, not a release sequence: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus were announced together on 4 March 2024 (Haiku shipped 13 March), Fable 5 launched before Sonnet 5 (30 June) and Opus 5 (24 July), and Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were disabled for all customers from 12 June until access was restored on 1 July 2026 (Mythos 5 only for approved US organizations) under a US export-control directive.

belief: Glasswing gave big tech early access to a defense model
corrected_statement: On 7 April 2026 Anthropic announced Project Glasswing, which gave gated access to Claude Mythos Preview, a general-purpose frontier model it decided not to release generally, to 11 named partners (Amazon Web Services, Apple, Google, Microsoft and NVIDIA, plus Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, JPMorganChase, the Linux Foundation and Palo Alto Networks) and over 40 other critical-software organisations, so they could find and fix software vulnerabilities, which is what "defense" means here (cyber defense, not a purpose-built military model). Glasswing was expanded by about 150 organisations on 2 June 2026, its successors Mythos 5 and 5.1 were still limited to vetted organisations when checked on 22 October 2026, and on 6 October 2026 Glasswing was folded into Anthropic's expanded Cyber Verification Program.
